item.title: 'Speak With Purpose is Seeking Board Candidates '
item.description:
'

Strong, dedicated voices can help shape a young person’s future.

Speak With Purpose is seeking board members ready to open doors, build meaningful partnerships, and champion youth voices. Our search is ongoing, and we would love to meet incredible candidates in person at our upcoming Board Orientation on Saturday, October 24, from 9:30–11:00 a.m. at White Center Hub.

Discover our work, explore board roles and expectations, and ask questions—then join our board for lunch and conversation.

RSVP by October 19 at 5:00 p.m. to Clarence Henderson at chenderson@speakwithpurpose.org. Unable to attend? We still welcome your interest. Please reach out to Clarence for more information.

Board roles and responsibilities: click here

item.title: 'Planting Party at Duwamish Hill Preserve'
item.description:
'

Join Dirt Corps, Serve Ethiopians Washington, Tukwila Parks, and Forterra in restoring essential habitat by planting a variety of native trees, shrubs, and a variety of prairie plants such as camas and lupine. We’ll start with a brief introduction to the site and have restoration professionals on hand to answer your questions. We’ll end with snacks and a special guest speaker sharing insights on the vital benefits of open space river corridors. Educational materials about the importance and history of the Duwamish River will also be available to take home.

'

item.title: 'Arbor Day at E.C. Hughes Park with Trees for Seattle'
item.description:
'

Join us as we celebrate Seattle Forest Week, fall planting season, trees, and our community at Arbor Day! We will be planting about 10 street trees along Southwest Holden Street as part of Arbor Day and the Safe Routes to School Program. Please bring your group, your family, or yourself and lend a hand to add canopy to our beautiful city. Tools, gloves, a light lunch and drinks will be provided.

'

item.title: 'Restoration Work Party at Duwamish Hill Preserve'
item.description:
'

Join Dirt Corps, Serve Ethiopians Washington, Tukwila Parks, and Forterra in restoring essential wildlife habitat by removing Himalayan blackberries that threaten our local native trees, shrubs, and groundcover at Duwamish Hill Preserve, a Tukwila park providing critical wildlife habitat and public trails in the middle of an industrial area. We’ll start with a brief introduction to the site and have restoration professionals on hand to answer your questions. We’ll end with snacks and a special guest speaker sharing insights on the vital benefits of open space river corridors. Educational materials about the importance and history of the Duwamish River will also be available to take home.

'

item.title: 'Volunteer Opportunity: Holiday Wrapping Party '
item.description:
'

Help us get holiday gifts ready for the community!

Join us at the United Way of King County office for a hands on volunteer experience where you’ll help wrap donated gifts and organize items for our nonprofit partners to shop for the people they serve.

You’ll spend the time wrapping, sorting, organizing, and getting donations ready to go. It’s a simple way to support local nonprofits and help make sure gifts reach community members who could use a little extra support this season.

What you’ll do:
• Wrap donated gifts
• Sort and organize donations
• Help prepare the space for our nonprofit partners
• Work alongside other volunteers to get everything ready for the season

Come ready to roll up your sleeves, wrap some gifts, and help make the holidays a little brighter for our community

'

item.title: 'Advocacy in Action: Support United Way at Seattle City Hall '
item.description:
'

With support from the City of Seattle in 2026, United Way was able to help our neighbors file for 5,449 returns, bringing back $6,200,000 in refunds for families! Show up in support as United Way of King County advocates for funding for our Free Tax preparation services in the Seattle budget for 2027. 

Background: 

The Seattle Mayor’s office recently released its 2027-2028 proposed budget, and over the next two months, the City Council will weigh community input as it decides what to prioritize before the budget is finalized around November 20th. 


The proposed budget funds many exciting programs that support our neighbors, but unfortunately, it does not include a key source of funding for United Way’s free tax preparation services in Seattle. We’re trying to change that, and we could use your help! 
 

What to Expect:
Join us at City Hall at 4:30 PM on 11/5 wearing a United Way shirt if you have one! We’ll try to have some additional sizes available, but it’s completely OK if we aren’t all wearing matching shirts.

Once we arrive, we’ll go through security and find seating in the audience. United Way of King County and a few of our community partners will take the microphone during public testimony to speak about the city budget and the importance of approximately $110,000 in funding for our 2027 free tax preparation campaign.

Our team and partners will be the ones speaking, so you do not need to prepare anything or speak yourself. We’re asking you to join us as a supportive audience and help show that this work has people behind it.

While we wait for our turn, you’ll also hear from other community members and organizations sharing what they need from the city budget. It’s a chance to see democracy and advocacy in action and to show up together for United Way and the community we serve.

Can’t make it in person?

We can still use your help! Use the council email to send a message directly to all of Seattle councilmembers: council@seattle.gov

'

item.title: 'International Rescue Committee's Annual Benefit Dinner, 21+'
item.description:
'

On Saturday, October 17th, IRC is celebrating its 50th year of serving refugees and immigrants in Seattle at our annual benefit dinner. To host this event, we need a strong cadre of volunteers. Please consider volunteering your time with us! We have roles available the night before, on Friday Oct. 16, and roles the day of the event on Oct. 17. All volunteering will be done at Pacific Tower in the Beacon Hill neighborhood of Seattle: 1200 S 12th Ave S, Seattle, WA 98144.The roles:

  • Friday Setup, 10/16, 7:30-9:30p: Setting up tables, chairs, and main layout for event. [2 more volunteers needed]
  • Saturday Parking/Elevator, 10/17, 4:15-6:15p: Parking, elevator volunteers (prepare for weather!) [8 more volunteers needed]
  • Saturday Food/spotting, 10/17, 4:45-9p: Ensure food is stocked, clear finished plates, prepare leftover containers, spotting for "raise the paddle" [8 more volunteers needed]
  • Saturday Teardown, 10/17, 8:30-10p: Take down and pack decor, put away tables and chairs, pack up event assets [6 more volunteers needed]

item.title: 'Fundraising Event Volunteer'
item.description:
'

Evening of HOPE Fundraising Event Volunteer

About YouthCare

YouthCare is a Seattle-based nonprofit dedicated to helping young people experiencing homelessness build stable, self-sufficient futures. For nearly 50 years, YouthCare has provided shelter, education, employment training, and trusted adult support to help young people find stability, pursue their goals, and thrive.

About Evening of HOPE

YouthCare’s inaugural Evening of HOPE is a special fundraising event bringing together community members, supporters, and advocates to celebrate the young people we serve and raise critical funds to support YouthCare’s programs and mission. We are looking for enthusiastic volunteers to help make this special evening a welcoming, organized, and memorable experience for our guests.

Volunteer Opportunity

Event volunteers will support the YouthCare team before, during, and/or after Evening of HOPE. Volunteers will be assigned to a variety of event support roles based on event needs and their interests and availability.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Helping set up the event space, including tables, signage, décor, and other event materials
  • Welcoming and checking in attendees and answering questions as needed
  • Supporting raffle activities and helping guests understand how to participate
  • Providing general event support as a floater
  • Helping with event tear-down and clean-up
  • Providing other support as needed throughout the evening
  • Specialized roles may include: Photography

Volunteers should be comfortable working as part of a team, interacting with guests and other volunteers, and jumping in wherever support is needed. No previous event or fundraising experience is required. YouthCare staff will provide direction and information needed for each volunteer assignment.

To Sign-up Visit: www.youthcare.org/volunteer or email volunteer@youthcare.org


Time Commitment

Evening of HOPE will take place on October 15th with volunteer shifts between 2:30pm - 9:30pm. Volunteer assignments will include opportunities to help with event set-up, during the event, and tear-down.

'

item.title: 'Board Treasurer (Volunteer), Beta OS'
item.description:
'

Why this role matters: Your independent oversight keeps every dollar accountable. That's how donors and funders keep trusting Beta OS, and how money keeps reaching technology that protects the endangered Southern Resident Killer Whales.

About Beta OS: Beta OS is a Washington nonprofit corporation that builds open source technology. It works with a collaborative group that works on the Orcasound website, where anyone can listen live to hydrophones in the Salish Sea. We're working with Orca Conservancy as our fiscal sponsor.

What you'll do:

  • Hold a board position. You'll be one of two members of the Beta OS Board of Directors, alongside me as Founder.
  • Review and approve compensation and expenses for Beta OS staff, as the director with no personal stake in those decisions.
  • Act as a signer on Beta OS bank accounts and review statements.
  • Keep financial records and give the board simple reports.
  • Advise on budgets, fiscal sponsorship and nonprofit financial practice.
  • Take part in board actions at least quarterly.

Who you are:

  • Experienced in accounting, bookkeeping, finance or nonprofit treasury.
  • Independent: not paid by Beta OS, with no family or business ties to its staff.
  • A member of a Tribe or First Nation in Washington, western Canada or coastal Alaska, or based in Western Washington, the Salish Sea, Victoria, Vancouver BC, the western Canadian coast and its islands, or coastal Alaska. Tribal and First Nations members are our highest priority.
  • Committed to Southern Resident Killer Whale conservation.
  • Nice to have: nonprofit board experience.

Commitment: remote. About 2 to 4 hours a week, sometimes more, sometimes less. The load varies.

Compensation: this is a volunteer role. No Beta OS board member is paid for board work.

How to apply: Fill out our Board Treasurer application form. It takes about 10 minutes. A resume, a cover letter and your LinkedIn profile link are required in addition to the form. Share your resume and cover letter as links in the form, or email them as attachments to brendan@orcasound.tech with the subject line "Board Treasurer application".

'

item.title: 'Seattle Ladies Choir- Concert Volunteers October 16th-17th'
item.description:
'

The Seattle Ladies Choir is made up of 50+ members with varying musical experience, from shower singers to professional musicians. It is a non-audition choir that strives to provide a supportive community for members and to connect through music.

Our concerts this season are Friday, October 16th and Saturday, October 17th. We are looking for volunteers to usher attendees to their seats, serve drinks and snacks at our concessions booth, and sell merch. Concessions volunteers must be 21+. Please sign up on our SignUp Genius page

Volunteers will be provided to a free ticket to the show for the same day they are volunteering or a different performance of their choice.

'

item.title: 'Wednesday Greeting Card & Supply Sorting for Seniors (Beacon Hill)'
item.description:
'

Do you enjoy organizing? Looking to put your skills to good use on Wednesday mornings or afternoons? 

Help sort our supply of greeting cards for isolated seniors in our ElderFriends program, donations, and other office supplies at the headquarters of our non-profit Full Life Care in South Seattle (Beacon Hill)! 

One-time volunteers and groups are welcomed, in addition to ongoing supporters; Additional organizational projects (event planning, paper filing, etc.) may be available according to your skills and interests. 

Other weekdays/times may be available upon request. 

Note: This service project is behind-the-scenes, not including clients. If interested in direct client interaction with our seniors, caregivers, and/or adults with disabilities, refer to our additional volunteer opportunities. 

'

item.title: 'Craft Winter Greeting Cards for Isolated Seniors (Remote)'
item.description:
'

Help brighten an elder's day using your card making supplies and creativity!

Handcraft general Winter themed greeting cards (not associated with any specific holiday) to donate to our nonprofit.

Sign up required; Click "Respond" to confirm your interest and receive card making guidelines (and event tips if hosting your own card making group), and instructions to mail or drop off completed cards at our South Seattle (Beacon Hill) office. Additional drop off locations further north may be available upon request. 

All cards created will be randomly distributed in December to Full Life Care's ElderFriends program participants. ElderFriends helps relieves loneliness and isolation among older adults in Seattle and greater King County, WA who may otherwise be alone this holiday season.

'

item.title: 'Help Prevent Furniture Waste at the South Transfer Station! '
item.description:
'

Furniture Repair Bank is a nonprofit effort that rescues worn, torn, and broken furniture from ending up in the landfill, restores its value and beauty, and provides it to people in need. Join our community of empathic, creative, and handy individuals! We conduct furniture collection events at the North and South Transfer Stations in Seattle, preventing furniture waste at the source. Dates will vary each month. 

Our truck, tent, and volunteers will be stationed outside the transfer station to divert residents who are planning to throw away usable furniture. Volunteer responsibilities include communicating the program to people lined up in their vehicles, and/or offloading furniture from the customer's vehicle and into our truck. After the event, we will deliver the collected items to our workshop in SoDo, Seattle. Volunteers may join for the collection event on-site at the Transfer Stations for a morning or afternoon shift. Please dress for the weather as this is an activity that takes place primarily outdoors.

Please dress for the weather as this is an activity that takes place primarily outdoors.

To volunteer for this opportunity, please register directly through the Furniture Repair Bank volunteer portal: Sign Up Here

'
